issues.legal_issue: Multiple electricity connections may be treated as clubbed connections when they are used in the same premises to avoid the tariff applicable to the combined load.
material_facts: Two electricity connections were found in a connected portion of premises, and the inspection report recorded that supply from one connection was being used on the other side.
The consumers maintained that the properties and connections were separate, relying in part on separate municipal property numbers and other documents.
The Electricity Board raised demands on the basis that the connections were liable to be clubbed.
issues.conclusion: The regulations and circular permit the Board to treat connections as clubbed and impose the applicable tariff and penalty if the connections are being used collectively in the same premises to evade the higher tariff; whether that was so here had to be determined on remand.
issues.legal_principle: The regulations framed under Sections 49 and 79(j) of the Electricity (Supply) Act, 1948, including clauses 3.5.2, 3.5.2.1 and 3.5.7, and the Board’s circular sought to prevent multiple connections in one premises from being used to avoid the tariff for the combined load. They must be interpreted to advance that purpose, and not to permit consumers to defeat it. No earlier cases are relied on.

rule.if: electricity_connection_clubbing_dispute and multiple_connections_in_one_premises and connections_used_collectively and intent_to_avoid_higher_tariff

predicates.electricity_connection_clubbing_dispute: A consumer challenged an electricity supplier’s demand based on treating multiple electricity connections as connected with the same premises.
predicates.multiple_connections_in_one_premises: More than one electricity connection was present in premises alleged to be the same premises.
predicates.connections_used_collectively: The consumer used electricity supplied through the connections collectively in the premises.
predicates.intent_to_avoid_higher_tariff: The consumer used the connections with the intention of avoiding the higher tariff applicable to the combined load.

issues.definition: When a consumer challenges a demand based on multiple connections in one premises, collective use of those connections to avoid the higher tariff permits the connections to be clubbed and the applicable charges to be imposed.

issues.legal_issue: An official inspection report is not to be rejected without cogent evidence rebutting its recorded facts.
material_facts: Electricity Board officers inspected the premises and recorded that the connections were in a connected portion and that some load from one connection was operating on the other side.
A consumer’s representative signed the report and received a copy; the report also bore an unspecified protest.
The consumers did not make specific objections identifying which recorded facts were incorrect, and the documents they relied on largely related to periods before the inspection.
issues.conclusion: The inspection report, prepared by officers in the discharge of their duties, carried a presumption in its favour; the consumers had to rebut it with proper and cogent evidence, and the report could not simply be disbelieved.
issues.legal_principle: An official document made by officers in the discharge of their duties is presumed to have been prepared in accordance with law. A party challenging its accuracy must rebut it with proper and cogent evidence. No earlier cases are relied on.

rule.if: electricity_connection_clubbing_dispute and official_inspection_report and consumer_challenges_report and not cogent_rebuttal_evidence

predicates.electricity_connection_clubbing_dispute: A consumer challenged an electricity supplier’s demand based on alleged use of multiple connections in the same premises.
predicates.official_inspection_report: Officers of the electricity supplier prepared a report recording facts during an inspection carried out in the performance of their duties.
predicates.consumer_challenges_report: The consumer disputed facts recorded in the official inspection report.
predicates.cogent_rebuttal_evidence: The consumer produced proper and cogent evidence showing that the report’s recorded facts were incorrect.

issues.definition: In a dispute over alleged use of multiple connections in the same premises, an official inspection report is presumed correct when the consumer disputes it but does not produce cogent evidence rebutting it.

issues.legal_issue: A dispute over whether multiple electricity connections are in the same premises requires fresh findings when the deciding forums have not adequately assessed conflicting evidence and the inspection report.
material_facts: The consumers relied on separate ownership, municipal property numbers and other documents to contend that the properties were distinct.
The inspection report recorded a connected portion and use of load from one connection on the other side.

The deciding forums reached different conclusions, and the appellate findings did not adequately explain why the inspection report should not be relied on or resolve whether the premises were distinct.
The Supreme Court considered that the record required a specific finding on whether the premises were distinct and whether the connections were being used collectively to avoid higher tariff.
issues.conclusion: The matter was remanded to the competent authority to make clear findings afresh, with the parties permitted to produce further documents; the notices and their consequences were subject to the final order.
issues.legal_principle: Where material facts concerning whether connections are in the same premises remain unresolved, the competent authority must record clear findings after considering the evidence, including the official inspection report and any cogent rebuttal. The Board’s regulations and circular cannot be rendered ineffective by an unexplained finding. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.electricity_connection_clubbing_dispute: A consumer challenged an electricity supplier’s demand based on alleged use of multiple connections in the same premises.
predicates.material_factual_conflict: The consumer’s evidence about separate premises conflicted with an official inspection report describing a connected portion or shared use of electricity.
predicates.lower_forums_failed_to_make_clear_findin: The forums deciding the dispute did not clearly resolve the factual conflict or explain their treatment of the inspection report.

issues.definition: When a connection-clubbing dispute contains a material factual conflict that the deciding forums have not clearly resolved, the matter must be remanded for fresh findings.
